A-1.notes: First floor plan (floor 1). Model floor 1 only. Include the street and alley entrances as `entrances` (floor 1): set `access_confirmed` to false when the sheet says access depends on a key, a gate or management, otherwise true. Each stair and elevator stop on this floor goes in `verticals` with one stop (floor 1).

A-2.notes: Typical floor plan that applies to floors 2, 3 and 5. Model it **once, as floor 2** (ids start with `f2-`, apartments `f2-apt-2a` and so on, labels as printed for floor 2 if numbered, else use 2A/2B/...). Another agent copies it to floors 3 and 5. Each stair and elevator stop goes in `verticals` with one stop (floor 2). No entrances on this sheet.

A-4.notes: Fourth floor plan (floor 4). Model floor 4 only. Each stair and elevator stop goes in `verticals` with one stop (floor 4). No entrances on this sheet.

A-301.notes: Stair section, not a plan: it shows which floors each stair serves and where each stair discharges or opens on each floor. There is no plan geometry here, so leave `layout` lists empty (`floors`, `spaces`, `openings`, `verticals`, `entrances` all `[]`) and put what you read in `section`. For render-and-compare, redraw the section (floor lines, shafts, labels) from your `section` JSON and compare it to the sheet.
A-301.extra_fields: "section": [ { "vertical": "stair-x", "label": "<as printed>", "floors": [1, 2, ...], "opens_to": { "<floor or floor range>": "<space name as printed>" }, "shares_shaft_with": "<vertical id or null>", "notes": "..." } ],
